title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 6 Lesson 1: Plane Pulley Hanging Mass custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $6\text{ kg}$ on a rough horizontal table with $\mu = 0.35$ is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $m$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum value of $m$ for which the system remains in equilibrium.

A block $A$ on a horizontal table is connected by a string passing over a smooth light pulley at the edge of the table to a hanging block $B$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$. The string is horizontal between $A$ and the pulley, and vertical between the pulley and $B$. The system is in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley.

A block $A$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline and supports a hanging mass $m_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the mass $m_B$ and the normal reaction $R_A$ on block $A$.

A particle on a plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal is connected via a smooth pulley at the crest to a vertically hanging mass. The tension in the string is $T = 40\text{ N}$. The string segment on the plane is parallel to the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley.

A block $A$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ with $\mu = 0.25$ is connected to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $m_B$. The block is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping up the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate $m_B$ correct to 3 significant figures.

A block of mass $3\text{ kg}$ on a rough horizontal table with $\mu = 0.4$ is attached via a string over a smooth pulley to a hanging mass of $2.5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 25\text{ N}$). A mass $m_\text{add}$ is placed on top of the block. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the minimum value of $m_\text{add}$ required to prevent the block from sliding.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal table. A light inextensible string is attached to $A$, passes over a smooth light pulley fixed at the edge of the table, and supports a vertically hanging particle $B$ of mass $m_B$. The string between $A$ and the pulley is horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the table is $\mu = 0.35$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction $R_A$ on block $A$, the maximum possible friction force $F_{\max}$, and the maximum mass $m_B$ of particle $B$ for which the system remains in equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When $m_B = 2.8\text{ kg}$, calculate the magnitude of the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $m_A = 5\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, with $\mu = 0.2$. A light string connected to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the slope and connects to a hanging mass $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension $T$ in the string and the normal reaction $R_A$ on particle $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude and direction of the friction force $F_f$ acting on particle $A$, and verify that particle $A$ remains in equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$ ($W_A = 40\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$ (so $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$). A light string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the crest and supports a vertically hanging body $B$ of mass $m_B$. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $\mu = 0.25$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the system is in limiting equilibrium with block $A$ on the point of sliding down the plane, calculate the normal reaction $R_A$, the maximum static friction $F_{\max}$, and the mass $m_B$ of body $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If body $B$ is replaced by a heavier body so that block $A$ is on the point of sliding up the plane, calculate the new mass $m_B'$ of the hanging body, and state the range of values of $m_B$ for equilibrium.

questions.prompt: For the system in the previous question when block $A$ is on the point of sliding up the plane ($T = 32\text{ N}$), the string segment on the slope is parallel to the line of greatest slope at angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal (where $\cos\alpha = 0.8$ and $\sin\alpha = 0.6$), and the other segment hangs vertically downwards.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally and vertically, calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R_P$ exerted by the string on the pulley correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the angle that this resultant force makes with the downward vertical correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $10\text{ kg}$ on a rough horizontal table ($\mu = 0.3$) is connected by a horizontal light string over a smooth pulley to a hanging mass $m_B = 5\text{ kg}$ ($W_B = 50\text{ N}$). To maintain equilibrium, an external force of magnitude $P$ is applied to block $A$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal directed away from the pulley. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving vertically, express the normal reaction $R_A$ on block $A$ in terms of $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When block $A$ is on the point of sliding towards the pulley, calculate the minimum force $P_{\min}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If $P$ is increased until block $A$ is on the point of sliding away from the pulley, calculate the maximum force $P_{\max}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $m_A = 8\text{ kg}$ ($W_A = 80\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, with $\mu = 0.2$. A light string connected to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the slope and connects to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $m_B = 2.5\text{ kg}$ ($W_B = 25\text{ N}$). A horizontal force of magnitude $H$ directed towards the incline pushes against block $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When block $A$ is on the point of sliding down the plane, express the normal reaction $R_A$ in terms of $H$, and calculate the minimum horizontal force $H_{\min}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If $H$ is increased until block $A$ is on the point of sliding up the plane, calculate the maximum horizontal force $H_{\max}$ correct to 3 significant figures, and state the range of values of $H$ for equilibrium.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $m_A = 6\text{ kg}$ on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with $\mu = 0.4$ is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the crest of the incline to a particle $B$ of mass $m_B = 4\text{ kg}$. A horizontal force of magnitude $Q$ is applied to particle $B$, holding it deflected so that the string segment between the pulley and $B$ makes an angle $\beta$ with the downward vertical. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces on particle $B$ vertically and horizontally, express the string tension $T$ and the angle $\beta$ in terms of $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum force $Q_{\max}$ that can be applied to particle $B$ before particle $A$ starts to slide up the inclined plane correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: When $Q = 31.3\text{ N}$, calculate the angle $\beta$ correct to 1 decimal place, and find the magnitude of the resultant force $R_P$ exerted on the crest pulley correct to 3 significant figures.
